title: Model catalog addition: GTM orchestration template and handoff matrix
creator: Aisha Bhattacharya
description: Create a reusable GTM orchestration template and living handoff matrix for adding new models to the Redwood catalog. This ticket produces: 1) a checklist for launch readiness across PM/ENG/DX/Legal/Support, 2) a canonical release-notes matrix mapping audience -> channels -> owner + snippets, 3) a benchmark and doc publish schedule, 4) a post-launch monitoring & rollback playbook. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc launches and ensure consistent quality, observability, and comms for model additions.
acceptance_criteria: A single Google Sheet + Confluence template exists with per-asset owners and deadlines
Release-notes matrix populated with templates for Public Blog, Console Release Notes, API Changelog, and Partner LOE
Benchmarks checklist includes latency P50/P95, throughput targets, and quality eval set references
Sign-off gates defined and linked (Legal, Security, Performance, Docs, Support)
Rollback and fallback policy documented with clear triggers and runbook links
checklist: Asset inventory: model card, benchmark deck, human-eval summary, sample prompts
Performance: run 50k token distribution perf tests, capture P50/P95 latencies and token cost delta
Quality: run 500-sample evals vs baseline and note regressions >5% on critical metrics
Security/Privacy: KMS verification for private variants + data retention note
Docs: draft API examples, console UX rows, quickstart snippet, migration notes
Release notes: craft short, medium, and long audience snippets (API, Console, Blog)
Communications: customer staging email list, external announcement draft, partner brief
Observability: dashboard created for model route, alerts for error rate & latency breaches
Canary plan: percentage ramping schedule (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and rollback criteria
Support: triage playbook and recommended categorization for incoming tickets
rollout_plan: Start with an internal alpha for Redwood employees (1 day), then gated canary to .hosted API customers using routing policy 'variant-canary' at 5% for 24 hours with active monitoring. If no regressions, ramp to 25% for 48 hours, then to 100% with regional stagger (NA -> EU -> APAC). Dedicated and Private customers: notify account owners and open scheduled maintenance windows before enabling; use feature flag for dedicated clusters.
release_notes_draft: Short: Added 'neo-lite-2' to the catalog — lower-latency option with comparable quality for short-answer tasks. Medium: Neo-lite-2 reduces median token latency by ~30% and is recommended for chat widgets and interactive UIs. Long: See benchmark appendix for trade-offs across sequence lengths and quantization settings; dedicated/private customers can request tuned variants via support.
monitoring_playbook: Create per-model route dashboard: latency, error-rate, cost-per-token, SLA burn
Alerts: P95 latency > 2x baseline for 10m; error-rate > 0.5% for 5m; cost-per-token > 150% expected
Auto-fallback: route to 'neo-stable' variant on sustained latency spikes
Post-mortem checklist: timeline, mitigation actions, root cause, follow-ups
post_launch_tasks: Collect customer feedback via CS touchpoints at Day 7 and Day 30
Run full 10k sample quality eval at Day 14 to detect data-drift/regressions
Finalize blog + case study drafts based on early usage signals
Audit cost trends and adjust batching/quantization recommendations
Lock down final changelog entry and archive pre-launch artifacts
decisions: Default console exposure level: 'beta' with opt-in toggle for all tenants
Benchmarks to publish: P50/P95 latency for 16/128/512 tokens and semantic similarity evals
Release cadence: catalog additions batched no more than 3 per week to reduce ops load
blockers: Security review outstanding: KMS integration doc needs completion (Omar)
Perf regression: initial quantized build shows P95 spike for long sequences (Priya investigating)
Design asset: sample prompt gallery needs localization guidance

Opportunity: If neo-lite-2 reduces cost-per-response by >20% for common chat lengths, Marketing wants an early case study.
